candidates.title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
candidates.description: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) models for autonomous driving use chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning to guide action generation, but incur substantial memory and computational costs. We study structured pruning for these models, focusing on preserving both scene understanding and trajectory prediction. Our analysis of Taylor importance in Alpamayo-1.5-10B shows that reasoning and trajectory objectives assign different importance to the same vision-language model (VLM) structures. In the action expert, MLP channels exhibit more stable importance rankings across denoising steps than query heads, and a small fraction of channels accounts for most of the measured importance. Based on these findings, we propose MoOP, which combines importance ranks from both objectives for VLM pruning and aggregates stepwise importance to select a fixed subset of expert MLP channels. At 24.0% total parameter reduction, VLM-only pruning with MoOP performs comparably to or slightly better than the strongest baselines in driving, while retaining 94.0% of the dense model's LingoQA score, far above all other methods. At a higher reduction of 30.0%, MoOP degrades much less than every other method, as it is the only one whose reasoning does not collapse. Removing 93.75% of expert MLP channels increases total parameter reduction to 39.4%, with nearly unchanged open-loop errors relative to VLM-only pruning and competitive closed-loop performance. The resulting model achieves a 1.37x end-to-end inference speedup and 36.6% lower peak memory than the dense model, without post-pruning fine-tuning.
candidates.author: Seongchan Kim, Soowon Son, Sangoh Kim, Hyunah Ko, Eunbeen Hong, Hyunkoo Lee, Sanghyun Lee, WonJun Moon, Kihong Kim, Dongyeon Son, Woongchan Nam, Seungryong Kim

candidates.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ
candidates.description: Prompting language models to verbalize stepwise numerical confidence during generation is an increasingly popular approach for triggering backtracking and error correction in agentic reasoning. This strategy presupposes two capabilities: (1) in-situ monitoring fidelity (does confidence drop when an error occurs?) and (2) downstream steering control (does an uncertainty token causally steer the model to repair its error?). We evaluated four open-weights models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, and Phi-4, 14.7B) across 15,200 math benchmark attempts, isolating 2,017 reasoning errors within each model's capability frontier. Applying 27,568 counterfactual continuations across these failure points, we demonstrate a consistent decoupling between monitoring and control. On monitoring, all four models fail to detect their own errors. Verbalized confidence does not distinguish mistake steps from sound reasoning, yielding near-chance within-position AUROCs between 0.500 and 0.561. Even at a model's first reasoning error, trajectory confidence remains saturated at 95.1% to 99.9%, with noticeable drops ($\ge 10$ points) appearing on fewer than 9% of errors in Llama and under 1.6% in the other three models. In contrast, models respond readily to external uncertainty: injecting a low-confidence tag (10%) at the error step significantly increases downstream correction across all models (+3.7 to +22.5 points over format-matched 95% certainty; all $p \le 0.0022$), reaching up to 38.5% under active rethinking instructions. However, injecting doubt onto already-correct steps causes models to discard valid reasoning, reducing solve rates by up to 22.8 points. Inference-time self-correction is thus bottlenecked by in-situ error detection rather than downstream repair capacity: models readily steer toward recovery when prompted with doubt, yet fail to self-monitor during generation.
candidates.author: Daniel Theron

candidates.title: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans
candidates.description: Radiology reports describe findings in text only, without visually marking them on the scan, so readers cannot directly see which abnormality each reported finding refers to. We introduce CTLink, a text-prompted 3D segmentation model that segments findings described in a chest CT report. CTLink was trained on 4123 noncontrast chest CT scans with 9547 segmented report findings, including ReXGroundingCTv2, a newly annotated dataset of 1134 scans and 1895 findings with every instance of each finding segmented. On the 200 ReXGroundingCT validation scans, CTLink achieved a hit rate of 0.816, an instance F1 score of 0.456, and a mean Dice score of 0.400, compared with 0.533, 0.175, and 0.234 for VoxTell, a publicly available text-prompted segmentation model (P < .001 for all). On the test set of the MICCAI 2026 ReXGrounding challenge, an ensemble of seven CTLink models achieved the highest hit rate (0.782) and instance F1 score (0.386) of all 48 participating teams. On 50 test scans segmented twice by independent radiologists, CTLink matched or exceeded inter-rater agreement. Diffuse non-focal findings remained the main limitation, partly because their extent is outlined inconsistently even between radiologists. The CTLink model weights are available at https://huggingface.co/rajpurkarlab/CTLink, and the dataset at https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGroundingCT.

candidates.title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
candidates.description: Humans explore unfamiliar spaces with purpose, deciding where to look until they have gathered the evidence a spatial question requires. However, can vision-language models (VLMs), which reason increasingly well over curated images and videos, also seek in space when the evidence is not handed to them? We present ActSpace-Bench, a benchmark of 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, where a model starts from a single view, navigates real captured frames, and must gather evidence before answering. To assess whether such exploration is purposeful, we introduce a controlled evaluation protocol that fixes each model as the reasoner and compares its own exploration against a same-budget random walk and an oracle route, separating evidence seeking from spatial reasoning. Every question is verified to require exploration and answered from 3D annotations, masked-evidence questions test whether models know when to abstain, and over 95% of sampled questions are confirmed correct by human verification. Evaluations of 23 proprietary, open-weight, and spatially specialized VLMs reveal that the strongest models do seek evidence with purpose but lose much of it to limited memory, whereas weaker and specialized models explore no better than a random walk or fail to reason over the evidence they are given, pointing to memory and evidence-grounded reasoning as the next targets for active spatial intelligence.
candidates.author: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xuhui Li, Xinlin Zhuang, Zhixiang Lu, Haolin Yang, Jianxu Chen, Yifan Lu, Zhiran Zhang, Yutong Xie

candidates.title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
candidates.description: Coding agents can construct and revise robot behavior during execution, but using one agent for the whole robot can delay otherwise independent work. We introduce Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP), an asynchronous framework that organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis, enabling asynchronous reasoning and execution. However, different robot components often have physical dependencies that require coordination. To address this challenge, ACAP introduces a hyper-agent that assigns tasks, coordinates dependencies, and dynamically allocates control between the lead and member agents. This allows independent work to progress concurrently while supporting tightly coupled manipulation when necessary. Across 72 real-world rollouts covering 25 task/platform settings, ACAP reduces task-balanced time cost by 28.2% compared with a single-agent Direct Policy, with improvements across Fully Parallel, Parallel-Sequential, and Collaborative tasks. Across all eight Collaborative settings, ACAP also achieves lower mean time cost than Fixed Delegation, where only member agents can control their assigned groups. An additional 90-rollout study shows lower mean 30-minute-capped time cost than Direct on all six tasks. We further demonstrate mobile manipulation using the same member interface for chassis and torso control. We present the framework and a real-world rollout dataset containing observations, generated programs, actions, and feedback to support research on how coding agents reason and act in the physical world.
candidates.author: Zexin He, Rui Li, Yushi Lan, Chengkai Jin, Zhi Hou, Xingang Pan

candidates.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
candidates.description: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe. This recipe prioritizes interfaces that exploit the model's native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors, and identifies effective choices for action representation, chunking, reasoning effort, visual observations, short multi-action sequences, and policy refinement. On RoboLab-120, Embo-Harness achieves an 83.3\% success rate, outperforming the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points. It also succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot trials across four real-world manipulation tasks. Beyond performance, controlled interventions indicate that the studied model depends more strongly on accurate spatial target estimation than on explicit low-level joint or trajectory generation. These results provide both a practical recipe for building strong frontier-model-as-policy harnesses and a clearer account of the capabilities that drive their performance.
candidates.author: Xiao-Ming Wu, Kang Liao, Yuexiao Ma, Taolin Zhang, Mingqian Zhou, Nuo Chen, Ziming Li, Yihang Luo, Rui Li, Zhonghua Wu, Tianyu Xie, Xiawu Zheng, Zhongang Cai, Zhi Hou, Chen Change Loy

candidates.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
candidates.description: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contrast, cope with insufficient tools by fashioning new ones from familiar parts and reusing them across tasks. Inspired by this, we propose ToolSmith, an automatic tool-generation framework that grows and reuses modules on top of a lean base tool library. We evaluate ToolSmith on three in-domain multimodal search benchmarks and ten out-of-domain benchmarks under a VLM-as-a-Judge protocol. ToolSmith consistently improves over the base library across deployed agents of varying scales, with larger backbones reaping greater gains, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. Our code and data are available at https://threesr.github.io/toolsmith/.
candidates.author: Rui Sun, Junhua Huang, Luca Zancato, Md Mofijul Islam, Kai-Wei Chang

candidates.title: VITA-WAM: Manifold-Aligned World-Action Modeling for Real-Time Robot Control
candidates.description: World action model (WAM) is a promising paradigm for visuomotor control by jointly modeling world dynamics and actions. Notably, existing WAMs often rely on large generative models and iterative sampling which incur substantial latency for action generation, limiting real-time deployment. In particular, there are two root causes of inefficiency in conventional flow matching or diffusion based action models in WAMs: 1) transporting uninformative Gaussian noise into precise actions necessitating multiple ODE steps, and 2) repeatedly injecting task context through expensive cross-attention modules. Our key insight is that jointly learning and aligning the source and action manifolds streamlines the transport between them, substantially accelerating action generation. Building on this insight, we introduce VITA-WAM, a WAM architecture with manifold-aligned flow-matching (VITA flow matching) that directly transports latent observation representations containing visual, language, and proprioceptive information into latent actions. More specifically, a flow latent alignment (FLA) mechanism is employed to facilitate manifold alignment between latent observation and action representations, enabling accurate generation with few ODE steps. The resulting architecture also eliminates costly attention for observation conditioning during repeated denoising steps. Notably, with a single ODE step, VITA-WAM outperforms 10-step FastWAM by 21.47 pp on LIBERO-Plus and by 1.65 pp on LIBERO, achieving these gains through the FLA objective without distillation, while inferring at 55.67~ms latency, a $2.10\times$ speedup compared to FastWAM.
candidates.author: Boqi Zhao, Dechen Gao, Hanchu Zhou, Hang Wang, Junshan Zhang

candidates.title: Learning Neurovascular Codes for EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis
candidates.description: In this paper, we introduce Neurovascular Codes as shared EEG representations for fMRI generation. We first train a separate EEG encoder to predict each fMRI signal, learning target-specific temporal and spectral features from the same EEG window. After training, we freeze the encoders and project their concatenated hidden features into a shared neurovascular code. Conditioned on this code, stochastic interpolant transforms Gaussian noise into a vector of fMRI signals, allowing different responses to be sampled for the same EEG window. We evaluate our approach on eight public simultaneous EEG-fMRI datasets, including four resting-state and four task-based datasets with 61,646 volume-level pairs. Under within-subject and held-out-subject evaluation, our model improves average Pearson correlation over the strongest encoder baselines by 19.1% and 19.8%, respectively. The corresponding improvements over the strongest generator baselines are 18.8% and 47.9%. Beyond reconstruction accuracy, we also evaluate the generated signals using subject-identification classifiers trained on real fMRI. Our method achieves the highest mean accuracy among the evaluated generators. We hope that our work opens up new opportunities for cross-modal brain modeling.
candidates.author: Yiming Sun, Yifan Wang, Aosong Feng, Yijia Ma, Ben Cheng, Xurui Wang, Yufan He, Yucheng Tang, Qing Lyu, Daguang Xu, Pei-Fen Kuan, Mingzhou Ding, Wen Li, Chenyu You

candidates.title: Know When to Abstain: Conformal Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL
candidates.description: Text-to-SQL systems often return queries that execute successfully but answer the wrong question. Detecting these errors at deployment is hard because execution correctness is defined against a gold query, which exists only in labeled data. We formulate confidence estimation for Text-to-SQL as probabilistic query validation under a latent correctness variable that is observable at calibration time through gold-SQL execution and latent at deployment. Our estimator separates generation from validation. A generator LLM writes and executes the query, and a different critic LLM judges the query and its execution result. The critic's validation and execution-grounded alignment scores are fused with the generator's verbalized confidence, token-level uncertainty, and SQL-structural features in a Random Forest, using two sequential LLM calls. Two calibration steps give finite-sample guarantees. A Learn-then-Test threshold ensures, with probability $1-δ$, that the error rate among accepted queries stays below a user-chosen budget. A conformal p-value bounds the false abstention rate. On Spider we use GPT-OSS-120B as generator and Gemma-4-31B as critic. The estimator obtains an AUARC of 0.899. Without abstention, 22.6% of queries are wrong. With a 15% risk budget ($δ=0.1$), a threshold is certified on all 10 resampled splits, and the system accepts 52.4% of queries on average with 9.1% observed error. Five different critic models give similar results. In a controlled comparison on Spider with Olmo-3-32B as generator, the estimator obtains an AUARC of 89.5, compared with 81.2 for the strongest logit-based baseline. Applied to BIRD without retraining, the confidence scores remain informative (AUROC 0.72, against 0.79 on Spider), but the risk guarantee does not transfer, as expected without exchangeability.
candidates.author: Avinash Kumar Singh, Bhaskarjit Sarmah, Stefano Pasquali

candidates.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
candidates.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) improves large language model search agents by up to 32 exact-match (EM) points over their pre-RL initializations, yet overall accuracy gains do not identify which underlying functional capabilities improve or interact during training. We introduce CO-GRAFT, a reward-agnostic interventional attribution framework in which an RL-trained agent and its pre-RL initialization jointly generate a single trajectory under closed-loop execution with live retrieval. Each policy controls a mutually exclusive subset of four functional roles: intermediate reasoning, search-or-answer decision, search query generation, and final answer extraction. Evaluating all 2^4=16 role assignments without modifying weights or retraining defines a cooperative game whose Shapley values decompose the total RL gain across roles, while M"obius interaction terms distinguish standalone role improvements from multi-role coupling. Applying CO-GRAFT to Search-R1 agents across Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.2 models (spanning two sizes, base and instruction-tuned initializations, GRPO and PPO optimizers, and NQ and HotpotQA datasets), we show that query generation never exceeds 15% of the total gain; instead, gains are governed by pre-RL answer validity, search retention, model scale, and fixed task-level search budgets, shifting credit from reasoning toward answer extraction in larger or well-formatted answer response checkpoints while smaller base models rely on reasoning--decision coupling.
candidates.author: Ramraj Chandradevan, Sayontan Ghosh, Vinoth Selvendran

candidates.title: Needwise: Generation-Free Conversational Recommendation from Need-Level Typed Decisions
candidates.description: Conversational recommenders must rank items against needs that catalogs record only in part, while users add, withdraw and reverse needs and switch between requests. LLM rankers re-read the dialogue at every turn: they are slow, and their ordering does not show which needs an item meets. We show that a conversational recommender can be built from typed decisions instead: named questions over fixed options, answered with option probabilities rather than generated text. On each turn, one typed request maps the message onto the catalog's fields, keeps what no field expresses in the user's words, and decides how the turn changes each earlier need. Needwise then ranks candidates must-first: the needs on the kind of item, its place and its price form a tier, and within it one holistic decision and need-level verdicts (supported, contradicted or unknown) are combined with equal weight (Needwise-HF). With the graded attributes withheld from the records, so that needs must be inferred from names, descriptions and reviews, Needwise-HF ranks Google Local requests significantly better than GPT-6 Sol (0.383 against 0.343 nDCG@10) and is not significantly different from the strongest LLM ranker on Google Local and Yelp; these comparisons keep their sign under every treatment of unrecorded attributes we test. It costs a fraction of GPT-6 Sol's API price and answers in 2.5 s at the median on Google Local, against 5.6 s for GPT-6 Sol. In conversations, the typed state keeps the ranking across switches and returns, but it recognizes only 19-27% of withdrawn needs.
candidates.author: Sungchul Kim, Weixiao Huang, Mekala Raja Sekhar Reddy, Amrutha Srinivasan
